summary: Balache Point light on the Gut of Canso was first lit 1 December 1905 and discontinued about 1955; its range lights date from 1963.

structures.note: First light on McMillan point, 32 ft to top of ventilator (Department of Marine, 1905 report).
Skeletal tower replaced the front light's wooden tower in 1991 (Lighthouse Friends); CCG list shows a square skeleton tower.
CCG list: white pyramid tower with red vertical stripe. Range lights established 1963 (Lighthouse Friends).

access.note: Grounds and tower closed (Lighthouse Friends). Owned by the Canadian Coast Guard.

events.note: Tower erected on McMillan point (Balache point), Gut of Canso.
Light put in operation 1 December 1905; fixed white dioptric, seventh order, 16 m high, visible 12 miles (the 1905 report says miles).
270-degree 5th-order French lens with duplex lamp, white (list of changes for 1907-8).
Lighthouse discontinued as the causeway neared completion; causeway completed 13 April 1955 (Lighthouse Friends).
Set of range lights established on Balache Point to guide vessels to the northern canal entrance (Lighthouse Friends).
Skeletal tower put in place for the front light (Lighthouse Friends).

corrections.why: The first light on McMillan point (Balache Point) was put in operation 1 December 1905 (Department of Marine). The 1963 date is for the range lights that now stand there, as Lighthouse Friends and the record's own event list show.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The current Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights gives Oc R 11s for both range lights, which decides the record's conflict in favour of the List over the other sources.
The record's 1963 build date (Rowlett) and the 1905 tower in the Department report are both right for different structures: 1905 is the first light, 1963 the range lights.

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-28 against the page images. The 1907 keepers' table (scan p. 151, printed p. 144) and the 1911 table (scan p. 244, printed p. 237) both place Chisholm on the McMillans Point line, with appointment 2 December 1905; the year is legible on the images but not in the OCR, so the 1911 OCR year was not used alone. The 1907 'Chisholm, John B' row was matched by line position beside McMillans Point; the image confirms it. Keepers after 1912 (McMaster, McLellan, A. Nicholson, C. Nicholson) rest on Lighthouse Friends alone and were not checked against Department tables. The 1905 report is for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1905 but was submitted in March 1906, and it records the 1 December 1905 light; the story says both. The 1908 list is headed as new lights erected during 1907-8 and changes made in existing lights; it prints 'McMillan s Point' (scan p. 96, printed p. 87) with a 270-degree 5th-order French lens. The 1905 report gives the range in miles, not nautical miles, so the story says miles. The 1963 range date and the 1955 causeway date come from Lighthouse Friends; no government source for 1963 was read. Lighthouse Friends spells the point 'Blanche' once; the story uses Balache. Rowlett's page was not fetched. No wreck or rescue at this point was found in the Marine report corpus; Chronicling America was not searched for this station. The record's 'access closed' matches Lighthouse Friends. The 1908 list gives a 270-degree sector, which differs from the 1905 'seventh order' fixed light; the reports do not say what replaced what, so the story says only that the apparatus had changed. The story now places the canal and swing bridge at the Cape Breton end of the causeway (Lighthouse Friends), not 'beside' it.
